source.stem:
A battery is connected to two crocodile clips and a lamp.
There is a gap between the crocodile clips.
Four cylinders W, X, Y and Z are made of the same metal but have different dimensions. The cylinders are connected in turn, by their ends, between the crocodile clips. The diagrams of the cylinders are all drawn to the same scale.
Which cylinder makes the lamp glow most brightly and which cylinder makes the lamp glow least brightly?

options.text: most brightly W; least brightly Y
most brightly W; least brightly Z
most brightly X; least brightly Y
most brightly X; least brightly Z

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Two cells always generate more heat than one cell, regardless of connection time.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: One cell generates more heat than two cells in the same wire over the same time.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Overheating at an electric iron's plug is useful heating.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Neither wire generates heat because neither wire glows.

intelligence.enrichment: For the same wire and duration, using two cells generates more heat than using one cell; the heating effect is useful in appliances but unwanted overheating can damage plugs, sockets, and appliances. more cells in the same heating activity -> more heat generated over the same duration; uncontrolled heating -> energy loss or damage; correctly rated wires, plugs, and sockets -> reduced unnecessary heating The learner correctly applies this rule: For the same wire and duration, using two cells generates more heat than using one cell; the heating effect is useful in appliances but unwanted overheating can damage plugs, sockets, and appliances. Any heating by electricity is useful, so more cells and hotter wires are always better.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Electricity: magnetic and heating effects. The student must decide: Compare how much heating occurs when the same wire is connected to one cell or two cells for the same duration, and judge whether that heating is useful or harmful in a situation. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
